dependence_surfaces.quote:
Deployed-row ids, roles and order are READ FROM specification.yaml frozen_curve_list (governing layer v1). change.D1_pins.rows lists the same ten ids in the same order; that list governs each row's source, parse rule and cross-checks only. The two lists were compared at design time and agree (design report). A run that finds them different stops in Stage P with outcome I_TEXT.
      controls:
        C-FIELD_cases_extracted:
          adds_to: controls[C-FIELD]
          item: DF-2
          path_name: controls[C-FIELD].cases_extracted
          rule: 'For EVERY row whose field prime was extracted in Stage P (whether or not the row pinned) there is one case, id CF-X-<row id>. Its value is that extracted field prime, taken from the Stage P record and not restated in any text. It is presented to the confounder check as an r with NO printed cofactor, so the hasse clause does not apply to it. Expected reason list: exactly [field_prime]. No integer of any such case is written in this text.'
          why_the_expected_reasons_are_fixed: Each extracted field prime is proved prime at run time (change.D7_certificates); hence not_prime does not fire. Under the corrected FP each value is a member of FP, so field_prime fires. The hasse clause does not apply because no cofactor is presented.
          mutation_sensitivity: If FP omits the extracted field prime of any row, that row's case is admitted and the gate below fails with outcome N2. In particular an FP built from the two C-FIELD expression values only (reviewer mutation M-FP of DEC-20260926-96f970 DF-2) admits every case whose row's field prime is not one of those two values, and the gate fails. The design-time locator run evaluated both FP definitions against these cases (execution-transcripts.json, pin_locators.fp_and_mutation).
        C-FIELD_gates_added:
          adds_to: controls[C-FIELD].gates
          item: DF-2
          gates:
          - Each case of cases_extracted must be rejected before any factoring, and its recorded reason list under the confounder check as written must be exactly [field_prime]. Any other result is outcome N2 (success_criterion N2_CONFOUNDER_CHECK_FALSIFIED reads "a C-FIELD case", which includes these cases).
          - 'Order of evaluation: the extraction_cross_check gate of every closed-form case (outcome I_TEXT on failure) is evaluated first, then the reason-list gates of all cases, closed-form and extracted. The results of cases_extracted are written to confounder_receipt.json under their own key.'
      tools:
        certificate_and_factoring_library:
          minimum_version:
            item: DF-3
            value: cypari2 2.1.5 with its PARI library 2.15.4
            rule: Admission item (1) requires the cypari2 distribution version to be at least 2.1.5 and the PARI library version reported through it to be at least 2.15.4. cysignals has no minimum version; its version is recorded, and admission item (3) decides whether the installed cypari2 and cysignals pairing can be admitted.
          version_command:
            item: DF-3
            command: python3 -I -c "<program>" with <program> equal to corrective.tools.version_program
            parse: Standard output, split on LF with the final empty string after the last LF dropped, must be exactly three lines. Line 1 is the cypari2 distribution version and line 3 the PARI library version; each must fully match [0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ . Line 2 is the cysignals distribution version, recorded as printed. A non-zero exit status, another line count or a non-matching line 1 or 3 FAILS admission item (1). Versions are compared as integer triples.
            why: No cypari2 release executed at design time defines cypari2.__version__ (execution-transcripts.json, cypari2_builds.*.typed_version_command_as_held). The distribution version comes from importlib.metadata and the PARI version from Pari.version(), whose first three entries are the PARI version integers.
          declared_builds:
            item: DF-3
            declared_minimum: cypari2 2.1.5, cysignals 1.11.4, PARI 2.15.4 (bundled), CPython 3.12
            declared_latest: cypari2 2.2.4, cysignals 1.12.6, PARI 2.17.2 (bundled), CPython 3.12
            gp_builds_probed: gp 2.15.4 and gp 2.17.4 (built from source), gp 2.17.3 (Homebrew)
            note: These are the builds on which admission items (1), (3) and (4) and the timeout recognition of change.D6_factoring.timeouts were executed at design time. Admission decides for any other build. The pairings cypari2 2.1.5 or 2.2.0 with cysignals 1.12.6 pass item (1) and FAIL item (3) (the child dies by signal), so admission refuses them as an infrastructure stop.
          stack_allocation:
            item: RI-7
            rule: 'Every cypari2 Pari instance that path A uses (factoring, primecert, primecertisvalid and high-precision evaluation) is created as cypari2.Pari(size=2**27, sizemax=2**32): an initial PARI stack of 2^27 bytes, allowed to grow to 2^32 bytes. A PARI stack overflow at that ceiling is a crash under stopping_rules, never a result.'
        version_program: import importlib.metadata as m, cypari2; p = cypari2.Pari(); print(m.version('cypari2')); print(m.version('cysignals')); print('.'.join(str(int(x)) for x in p.version()[:3]))
        version_program_sha256: 5701a5e33b9bb8e413374fbdd4715ec3fc08f442d589a7080694b4eab0709dc5
        alarm_self_test_program: "import cypari2\nfrom cysignals.signals import AlarmInterrupt\np = cypari2.Pari(size=2**27, sizemax=2**32)\nfor e in ('alarm(1, while(1, ))', 'alarm(1, factor(nextprime(2^140)*nextprime(2^141)))'):\n    try:\n        p(e)\n        print('RETURNED')\n    except AlarmInterrupt:\n        print('ALARM')\nprint(p('2+2'))\n"
        alarm_self_test_program_sha256: fb9b43c9ba30c664e436a6ef945fd0ca6a3a3196773b1be15dde8aefe6075776
        program_hash_convention: sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the string value as a YAML safe loader returns it (the second program ends with one LF, the first with none).
        admission_gate_items_added:
          adds_to: tools_and_admission.admission_gate
          item: RI-7
          items:
          - (9) Execution audit. The AST audit of admission item (6) also FAILS if any module under experiments/EXP-AUXIN-92dccc/implementation/typed/ calls exec, eval, compile or __import__, imports runpy, or uses importlib other than importlib.metadata. Code from any repository file outside experiments/EXP-AUXIN-92dccc/implementation/typed/ is never executed by any route, whether import, exec or loading by path.
          - (10) Environment location. The resolved sys.prefix of the admitted interpreter and the resolved file path of every installed third-party distribution module lie OUTSIDE the repository working tree. An environment inside the repository fails admission, because its modules would be both allowed (import_rule class b) and forbidden (inside the repository, outside experiments/EXP-AUXIN-92dccc/implementation/typed/).
      custody:
        run_entry_sys_path:
          adds_to: change.D8_custody.import_rule
          item: RI-7
          rule: Under python3 -I the directory of run.py is NOT on sys.path (executed at design time on CPython 3.10 and 3.12; execution-transcripts.json, isolated_mode_sys_path). run.py therefore inserts the absolute path of experiments/EXP-AUXIN-92dccc/implementation/typed/ at sys.path[0] before its first import of any module under that directory, importing only sys and os before doing so. That is the only change to sys.path the run makes, and it is recorded in import_audit.json.
        invalidation_rules_added:
          adds_to: invalidation_rules
          rules:
          - Any edit of AMD-20260927-narrow.yaml after approval - evidence-integrity failure.
          - Any byte difference between AMD-20260926-typed.yaml and the sha256 in incorporates.sha256 - evidence-integrity failure.
      bin_by_status:
        replaces: change.D3_descriptive_bins.bin_by_status
        item: DF-6
        text: 'For every branch of every deployed row, construction control, C-BOUND state and null-arm sample, three fields are reported: bin, bin_at_least and boundary_flag, each with exactly the value given here. EXACT: bin is given by definitions.bins; bin_at_least equals bin; boundary_flag is as definitions.bins defines it. BOUND: let s be the depth of the witnessed upper bound and boundary_flag the flag that definitions.bins computes on s. If boundary_flag is false and s >= 3/4 + tau, bin is NEAR_FLOOR and bin_at_least is NEAR_FLOOR (the true value is at least as deep). Otherwise bin is UNDETERMINED and bin_at_least is the bin that definitions.bins gives an EXACT value of depth s (so a witnessed depth within tau of 3/4 gives UNDETERMINED, bin_at_least INTERMEDIATE and boundary_flag true). VOID: bin, bin_at_least and boundary_flag are all null. UNPINNED rows have no branches and report none of the three. This clause and definitions.bins never give two answers, and no status and bin
          combination leaves bin_at_least undefined.'
        totality_table:
        - status: EXACT
          bin: NEAR_FLOOR
          bin_at_least: NEAR_FLOOR
        - status: EXACT
          bin: INTERMEDIATE
          bin_at_least: INTERMEDIATE
        - status: EXACT
          bin: NEAR_CEILING
          bin_at_least: NEAR_CEILING
        - status: BOUND
          bin: NEAR_FLOOR
          bin_at_least: NEAR_FLOOR
        - status: BOUND
          bin: UNDETERMINED
          bin_at_least: INTERMEDIATE or NEAR_CEILING (the EXACT bin of s)
        - status: VOID
          bin: null
          bin_at_least: null
        - status: UNPINNED
          bin: none reported
          bin_at_least: none reported
      interpretation_limits_item_6:
        replaces: interpretation_limits item 6 (the item beginning "On the two pairing-family rows")
        item: DF-5
        text: BN254-r and BLS12-381-r are reported in their own stratum (expected_structure_flag true, change.D3_descriptive_bins.stratification). No status, bin, depth or other category is predicted for them, and no value on them is read as family-caused.
        reading_of_the_held_stratification_parenthetical: The parenthetical in change.D3_descriptive_bins.stratification (the two rows "whose family polynomials force divisors, CORR-20260923-187ea3") stays incorporated.         adds_to: change.D4_calibration.threshold_inventory
        item: RI-5
        constants: 'Admission timeouts: 600 seconds for the ECM self-test (item 2) and 10 seconds of wall clock for the alarm self-test child (item 3); the alarm length A = 1 second inside that self-test. Minimum tool versions: GMP-ECM 7.0.4; cypari2 2.1.5 with PARI 2.15.4; pypdf 3.0.0 (held); Python 3.10. PARI stack: initial 2^27 bytes, ceiling 2^32 bytes. The screen''s optional trial-division bound of at most 2^16 (conventions.Q0-5). PR-SEC2''s continuation minimum of 4 characters. PR-EIP197''s required match count of exactly one. The PDF short-string length 20 of corrective.pins.pdf_digit_check_weakness (a reporting label, no stop). Expected sha256 digests and byte counts of the two pinned-revision files (equality tests, no cut-off). No constant in this list reads a deployed-row or null-arm outcome, and each was fixed before any such outcome existed.'
      falsification_condition_mapping:
        item: RI-1
        rule: Each falsification condition of H-AUXIN-6db354 (in its listed order, FC1 to FC6) is mapped to the outcome of this protocol that decides it. None is retired. Two are demoted, with reason.
        rows:
        - fc: FC1 (a constructed control fails a gate)
          outcome: N1_INSTRUMENT_FALSIFIED
          status: kept
        - fc: FC2 (a field prime presented as r is admitted)
          outcome: N2_CONFOUNDER_CHECK_FALSIFIED
          status: demoted in part
          reason: 'The controls can present only field primes that the text or Stage P makes available: the two closed-form C-FIELD cases and every extracted field prime (cases_extracted). A field prime of a curve outside the frozen list, or one no locator extracts, cannot be presented, so FC2 is decided for the extracted set only. A deployed row whose own r equals a member of FP is invalid_measurement for that row (held invalidation rule), not N2.'
        - fc: FC3 (a reported exponent or bound below its analytic floor, or T_plus(d) < d)
          outcome: N3_FLOOR_VIOLATION
          status: kept
        - fc: FC4 (reported prime factors of an EXACT branch do not multiply back)
          outcome: N1 when the branch belongs to a construction control (its EXACT gate fails); for a deployed or null-arm branch the product check makes the branch VOID (C-PRODUCT; held invalidation rules), which gives S_PARTIAL_TABLE
          status: demoted
          reason: On a deployed or null-arm branch a product mismatch shows a defect in that branch's factorization record, not in the instrument as a whole, so this contract's stated rule voids the branch instead of falsifying the instrument. On construction controls, where the correct factorization is fixed by the recipe, it falsifies the instrument as H states.
        - fc: FC5 (a declared-state BOUND evaluator control returns a value other than the one fixed)
          outcome: N4_BOUND_EVALUATOR_FALSIFIED
          status: kept
        - fc: FC6 (a row omits either branch)
          outcome: The row is incomplete, not negative. specification.yaml tail_checks item 1 (v1, "a missing branch voids the row") makes each omitted branch VOID, which gives S_PARTIAL_TABLE; an omission caused by a crash is I_INFRA.
          status: kept (as H states it, incomplete and not negative)
      reviewer_convention_zero_runs:
        item: RI-9
        convention: At zero runs a reviewer reads each gate that needs a pipeline factorization (the blind EXACT status of a construction control, the F3 routing observation of C-PLANT-PL) as a RUN OBSERVATION. Its text is judged determinate when the expected value is fixed by the text alone (change.D5_controls.expected_status_convention); whether the pipeline attains that value is not reviewable before a run and is neither a pass nor a break of the text.

Editing a construction-control field would reopen regression group R-D4, which held twice. Revisit when any later amendment edits C-PLANT-PL for another reason.

The split of the label into the 2010 source''s two cases cannot be written by this session, which has not read that source (a recalled reference would be a pointer only); and D2 lies in regression group R-D2D3. The typed costs, which the label annotates, are unchanged. Revisit: a later card whose producer has read the 2010 source and records it as retrieved.'
